thread:
grace: Noticing intermittent packet loss on overlay in prod-west affecting model-serving RPCs. Tail errors show a bunch of `write: broken pipe` and probe logs with high retransmit counts. Started ~03:10 UTC, repeating every ~10-15m.

maria: Thanks, can you paste the small pcap or tcpdump snippet? Any correlation with GPU pod noisy neighbors or evictions?

grace: Pcap attached (small sample). No evictions. GPUs stayed pinned. Pods on same node talking over geneve overlay. Logs: `rpc: timeout waiting for response`, kube-proxy conntrack shows retransmits.

alex: Quick checklist: MTU mismatch, GSO/GRO offload weirdness, NIC driver logs, and geneve offload interaction. After last kernel update we've seen GSO failures on encapsulated tunnels.

samir: Ran `tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/geneve-sample.pcap 'tcp and host 10.44.12.34'` for 30s. Captured a burst where sender retransmits 8 packets then recovery. Also saw duplicate ACKs from receiver.

maria: Can you dump `ethtool -k` on the physical NIC and the geneve interface? Also `ip -s link show geneve0` and `cat /proc/net/softnet_stat` counters.

grace: ethtool -k on NIC: `offload: tx-checksum on, gso on, tso on, gro on`. geneve interface shows `gso on, gro on`. softnet_stat shows spikes in dropped packets in bucket 2 at the same timestamps.

alex: That's consistent with GSO/GRO getting confused by geneve encapsulation. Kernel might hand off a large GSO frame to the NIC which can't handle the encaps size -> payload dropped -> stack sees retransmits.

maria: Quick mitigation to test: disable GSO/GRO/TSO on geneve and host NIC temporarily. Commands: ```
# on host
ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
ethtool -K geneve0 tso off gso off gro off
sysctl -w net.core.gso_max_size=0
```
Keep an eye on CPU. This will increase packet count and CPU but should eliminate the broken-offload path.

samir: Did the temporary disable on a canary node. Within 2 mins retransmits dropped to near zero for that pod pair. Tail RPC errors stopped in that pod. CPU on that node went up ~6%.

grace: Nice. So likely offload bug/regression with geneve encapsulation and current NIC driver/kernel combo. Which kernel roll did we land last week?

alex: Kernel 5.15.88 -> 5.15.92-ish range got a net patch for GSO split handling; still flaky on some Broadcom/Mellanox drivers. Need to check dmesg for `NETDEV WATCHDOG` or GSO failure messages. I saw `gso: failed to split skb` in dmesg on the canary.

maria: Also check `ethtool -S eth0 | grep gso` for driver counters. If driver has tx_dropped_on_gso or similar it points at the NIC.

grace: ethtool -S shows `gso_err: 14` on the affected host. dmesg snippet: `mlx5_core: GSO split error on encap skb, len=high, dma mapping failed`.

samir: We have two viable paths: 1) Rollback kernel/driver to previous known-good (costly across fleet), 2) Keep offloads disabled on overlay-carrying nodes until upstream fix + backport driver patch. 3) Try forcing geneve to use GRO
doable?

alex: Forcing gro would still hit the same bug if encaps size exceeds limits. Best short-term is disabling offloads on nodes that run GPU-model-serving pods (pin as pod-level label + daemonset to set ethtool). We can automate with node-feature-daemon or a small init container that sets offloads on startup.

maria: Suggestion: create a conservative rollout: start by rolling the ethtool change via a DaemonSet that checks kernel/driver and toggles offloads only on nodes where `gso_err` counters > 0 or where geneve is in use. Add a feature flag to Redwood infra to revert quickly.

infra-bot: Deploy window suggested: start 2024-09-17 04:00 UTC for minimal traffic. Estimated impact: +3-8% CPU on affected nodes, increased packet rate.

grace: I'll draft the DS and a runbook. Need to add monitoring: alert on `gso_err` > 0 and on `tcp_retransmits` spike at pod level. Also add a synthetic probe between two sample GPU pods in each AZ to detect recurrence.

samir: Also tested a local kernel param tweak `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` — helped a little on recovery but didn't eliminate packet drops. It's a complementary mitigation.

alex: Long term: backport NIC driver fix or upgrade kernel + vendor driver, and validate with encapsulated GSO stress tests. Also evaluate moving some heavy east-west flows to hostNetwork for critical paths if overlay can't be relied on (tradeoffs: security/isolation).

maria: For the DS, I'll include commands and a quick revert label. DS will run `/sbin/ethtool -K $IF tso off gso off gro off` for listed interfaces and annotate node with `overlay-offload=disabled`.

grace: After canary DS on 2 nodes: no more RPC tail errors observed for 4 hours. I'll open a CH ticket to coordinate kernel/driver rollback path and soak tests.

alex: Good work. Follow-ups: collect a handful of pcap samples, ethtool -S dumps, and dmesg from affected nodes and upload to the incident case. We'll coordinate with vendor for a driver patch.

maria: I'll push the DS PR and a dashboard for `gso_err`, `tcp_retransmits`, and per-pod tail RPC error rate.

grace: Thanks team :thumbsup: keeping this thread for postmortem notes and next steps.
